chunk-001:c003.proposition: Origin-of-life inquiry should remain a fair, evidence-grounded scientific debate, while intelligent design lacks a demonstrable scientific basis.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin independently defines the scientific scope of inquiry by rejecting intelligent design and calling for a fair, well-grounded evidentiary debate.

chunk-001:c004.proposition: Laboratory work can reveal a gradual pathway by which simple chemistry generates complexity capable of evolution without recreating Earth's exact history.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin affirmatively presents laboratory discovery of general chemical laws and a gradual transition toward evolution as the relevant explanatory pathway.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: Meteoritic and early-Earth evidence supports a simpler chemical starting world while leaving the precise sequence of prebiotic molecules unresolved.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin expressly combines positive evidence for simple early chemistry with a limitation: there is no evidence fixing a detailed molecular sequence.

chunk-001:c008.proposition: Syntactically structured information requiring encoding and decoding can mark the transition from ordinary chemistry toward agency or decision-making systems.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin independently identifies encoding, decoding, agency, and decision-making as observable features for investigating the transition from chemistry toward life.

chunk-002:c002-02.proposition: The molybdate system exhibits molecular templating and a coupled set in which catalysts help generate other catalysts, exceeding ordinary autocatalysis.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin describes the system's hierarchical templating and mutually connected catalyst production as concrete experimental properties distinct from simple self-promotion.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: An informational-complexity assay can experimentally distinguish biological organization from random chemistry without reconstructing Earth's unique historical pathway.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin proposes a black-box assay that distinguishes a living cell from random chemistry, supplying an independently testable operational measure.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: Simple generative laws may underlie life-like complexity even when those laws are obscured by the intricacy of modern cellular systems.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin's gravity analogy independently supports studying simple system-level regularities rather than treating the modern cell's full complexity as the necessary starting point.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Simple molybdate chemistry can produce improbable templated structures and coupled catalytic organization without engineered biological sequence information.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin grounds the proposition in naturally occurring small templates, sodium molybdate, and the reported emergence of coupled catalytic sets outside biology.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: A permissive environment may enable primitive self-copying chemistry to arise, after which selection can develop increasingly functional molecular organization.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin supplies a standalone staged mechanism linking a forgiving chemical environment, primitive copying, selection, and later functional polymers.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-004.proposition: An objective measure of molecular complexity can support a theory in which chemical evolution generates organized complexity beyond already biological systems.

orphanFallback.rationale: Cronin independently invokes a developing theory that objectively measures molecular complexity and extends evolutionary organization into chemistry.
